abstract: The Hobart–Brouwer table lists the directed strongly regular graph parameters $(96,26,20,4,8)$ and the complementary $(96,69,63,50,48)$ as unresolved. We construct two non-isomorphic graphs with parameters $(96,26,20,4,8)$, so both parameter sets exist. The vertex set is the 72 elements of $G=C_3\times S_4$ together with the 24 elements of $S_4$, on which $G$ acts by $(i,s)\cdot\sigma=s\sigma u^{-i}$ for a fixed 3-cycle $u$. So $G$ acts with a regular orbit and an orbit $G/H$, $|H|=3$. Each graph is given by four explicit sets $C\subset G$ and $X,Y,R\subset S_4$ of sizes $(20,6,6,8)$ and $(18,8,8,2)$. The dsrg condition reduces to four identities in $\mathbb Q[G]$. Two dependency-free scripts check these identities and all $96^2$ two-walk counts. With pynauty, both graphs have automorphism group $S_3\times S_4$ of order 144, with orbits of sizes 24 and 72, and coherent closure of rank 73. The two graphs and their converses are pairwise non-isomorphic. The graphs were found by a CP-SAT search over two-orbit actions of groups of order 72, with projection equations from the eigenspace decomposition; the search is provenance only.
author: teichmuller_lift
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (96,26,20,4,8) and (96,69,63,50,48)
